name: Blackwood Camp
summary: Blackwood Camp is a small furbolg settlement nestled along the coast of Darkshore south of Auberdine. Once peaceful allies of the night elves, the Blackwood tribe residing here has fallen into violent madness under a sinister demonic taint.

sections.title: A Tribe in Madness
sections.body: The Blackwood furbolgs long coexisted peacefully with the night elves of Auberdine, sharing reverence for nature and guarding the coastal woodlands. In recent times, however, an unnatural corruption seeped into their settlement, twisting their minds and turning them fiercely aggressive toward all outsiders. Driven to desperation and rage, the tribe attacked travelers and severed all ties of kinship. Night elf sentinels and druids watch the settlement with deep grief, searching for a way to break the dark hold gripping their former friends.

sections.title: The Satyr's Shadow
sections.body: The true cause of the tribe's downfall is not natural madness, but the malevolent scheming of a satyr hiding in the shadows of Darkshore. Through foul demonic magic, the creature poisoned the furbolgs' minds, binding them in misery and hostility. Night elf ritualists seek to slay the offending satyr and enact ancient purification rites, hoping to cleanse the Blackwood tribe before their corruption becomes irreversible.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs at Blackwood Camp hostile?
faq.answer: The Blackwood furbolgs are suffering from a dark demonic curse cast by a local satyr. This foul magic warped their minds, driving them to blind aggression against anyone who approaches.

faq.q: Can the Blackwood furbolgs be saved?
faq.answer: Yes. Night elf allies in Darkshore provide rituals to confront and slay the corrupting satyr, allowing sacred purifications to cleanse the furbolgs of their madness.
The camp lies along the coast of Darkshore, situated south of the port town of Auberdine.

faq.q: What was the tribe's historical relationship with the night elves?
faq.answer: Before the Third War and the recent wave of demonic taint, furbolg tribes such as the Blackwood maintained peaceful and cooperative relations with the night elves, sharing mutual respect for the natural world.

angles.text: For the Kaldorei, the madness at Blackwood Camp is a tragedy hitting close to home, as former allies of the wilderness have fallen victim to lingering demonic corruption.
Druids view the affliction of the Blackwood tribe as a spiritual infection demanding both decisive martial action against demonic manipulators and compassionate cleansing rites.
